runtime_prompt_en:
A candid editorial photograph in a tiny neighborhood grocery on a dry overcast morning. One adult woman shopper stands close to a low wooden shelf of cooking oils, comparing two similar olive oil bottles in a single visible moment of choice. Her left hand holds a green glass olive oil bottle and her right hand holds an amber glass olive oil bottle; she brings their front labels side by side at chest height, angles both labels toward herself, and studies them with a concentrated downward gaze. The bottles remain separate and equally visible, with the colored glass and matching olive oil bottle shapes making their similarity and difference clear. Her long dark wavy hair parted near the center, dark eyes, and softly contoured face take only visible appearance guidance from the attached portrait. She wears a charcoal cardigan over a simple pale shirt. A blue wire shopping basket rests on the counter below her elbows. Narrow shelves of bottled sauces continue behind her, while cool fluorescent strips and gray window light define the compact working shop. Frame her face, both hands, both bottle bodies and labels, the basket, and the shelves together in an eye-level three-quarter photograph; preserve plausible grips, supported posture, and crisp product-to-hand contact. Two comparable products are simultaneously visible at one shopping area, their shared bottle silhouettes and two glass colors clear against the oil shelf. The shopper holds one product beside the second alternative, maintaining equal front-label exposure as she considers the pair. The shopper's hand or gaze connects both products as one choice: her eyes follow the two adjacent front panels while her hands bring them to the same depth. The compared products have visible support from hands, basket, or shelf: here each raised bottle is gripped by a different, fully visible hand with its cardigan sleeve continuing into the wrist. From the shopper's anatomical viewpoint, her left hand and green bottle appear on frame right, and her right hand and amber bottle on frame left; show both sleeves leading continuously into their grips. Use a normal 50 mm view with depth of field keeping eyes, hands, and bottle labels sharp together.

Avoid: body distortion, broken facial features, 3D render look, over-processed retouching, unrealistic hands, distorted fingers, cartoon style, illustration look
